chapter: Jump for Joy, records and royalties
title: The skit 'Sh, He's on the Beat'
summary: Turner played a policeman who walks in on a club, intending to sit in; he can't recall the song he sang.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Uh, when I...when I was here before with the program from "Jump For Joy," you remembered...uh, something about a skit you were in called, "Shhhh, He's On The Beat." You were a policeman, right?
Yeah. Yeah, I was a policeman on...on.."He's On the Beat."
What do you remember about that skit?

Oh, it was more talk than it was anything. The way I was doin' it, I was...they had a...looked like a window. I was walkin' up past the joint. You could...all you could see was my feet goin' back and forth, so I come in the joint. They thought I was goin' to raid 'em. I heard the music, and I come on down in the joint, and there was supposed to...there was a scene like I was gonna raid 'em. I told 'em, "Don't worry about that. I ain't gonna put you in jail. I only wanta sit in wit' your boys and play some of this good music." And I started off to singin'. Therefore, that's how that went down.
Do you remember what you sang in that scene?
Do you remember what you sang in that scene?
No, no, been too long ago. There was a whole lot

of different songs that I wrote but I don't remember them now. I run through them old records of mine, I got them old 78s, and my wife picks 'em out for me now, and sometime I'm doin' a session...ain't got nothin' to sing. I go back and pick up all those old numbers that I did years ago, and people think they're brand new, and I had already did 'em.
